exposure: Eating disorders stratified by subtype (anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa, EDNOS)
cohort: 7542 women with eating disorders and 1,225,321 women without eating disorders, identified from the Swedish Medical Birth Register (2003-2014)
finding: Women with active or previous eating disorders, regardless of subtype, have an increased risk of adverse pregnancy and neonatal outcomes, including hyperemesis gravidarum, preterm birth, and microcephaly.
mod_finding: Women with anorexia nervosa and EDNOS had a decreased risk of instrumental-assisted vaginal births.
birth_weight: Small for gestational age, large for gestational age
